messages.author: 4f782baffe1b9d1a
messages.subject: Re: Analysis > Correlation reset button
parts:
Hi, Bruce,

It depends a bit on the format you'd like to have in the output.  DeducerRichOutput provides the option of saving just results (output) as HTML.  To do that, you would select File -> Save, and then move the radio button at the bottom from "Complete Output" to "Results".  I would recommend giving the file name the .html extension.  You can then open that file in any browser to view your results later.  It sounds like you don't want just the printed results but rather output that can be processed further?  To do that, you'll need to save the R objects that are produced during analysis.

One limitation of RichOutput is that it over-rides some commands from Deducer to print results directly to the console without generating any R objects.  An example of such a command is descriptive.table.  If you try:

> getAnywhere(descriptive.table)

with RichOutput loaded, R will tell you that there are two versions of it, one in Deducer and one in DeducerRichOutput.  It sounds like you want the one in Deducer, which will produce an R object at the end.  To do that, modify the descriptive.table command so that it uses Deducer's descriptive.table function (I'm using a data set I had handy):

> xyz <- Deducer::descriptive.table(vars = d(w_att_m,w_resp_m,m_att_w,m_resp_w) ,
    strata = d(courtesy),data= chivttest,
    func.names =c("Mean","St. Deviation","Valid N"))

I usually use the save command instead of dput:

> save(xyz, file = "C:\\R\\descriptives.robj")

You can close R, restart it, and do:

> load("C:\\R\\descriptives.robj")

and you should now have an object called xyz available that contains all the output.

Hope that helps,
--Bill
